title: Data center companies agree with Duke Energy and customer advocates to pay more for electricity
source_used: Duke Energy press release (PR Newswire, via Yahoo Finance); IndexBox summary
key_facts: Duke Energy Carolinas, Duke Energy Progress and the North Carolina Public Staff reached a settlement on 7 Oct 2026 on costs of serving data centers and other large loads.
Other parties: Amazon, Google, Meta, Microsoft, the Carolina Industrial Group for Fair Utility Rates and the US Department of Defense.

Large customers must make nonrefundable upfront payments for grid facilities serving only them (e.g. a substation) and post deposits and security for upgrades serving all customers (e.g. transmission lines).
New large-load customers, including new data centers, must take service under a separate High Load Factor rate schedule.

Applies to customers of 50 MW or more with an 80% load factor that sign an electric service agreement after 1 Jun 2026; earlier agreements carry similar protections; the earlier rule covered loads of 100 MW or more.
Needs North Carolina Utilities Commission approval; decision expected by mid-November.
Duke serves about 3.9 million customers across its two North Carolina utilities, which merge on 1 Jan 2027.
quote_evidence: It's simple – data centers will pay upfront for all costs to connect to the grid,” said Kendal Bowman, Duke Energy's North Carolina president.
The agreement is subject to approval by the North Carolina Utilities Commission – a decision is expected by mid-November.
Nonrefundable, upfront payment for electric grid facilities serving only that customer, such as a substation to connect to the grid.
why_it_matters_hint: Sets a template for making data centers, not other customers, pay to connect to the grid.
notes: Company-origin announcement; WSOC TV, News & Observer and others carried it. Pending regulatory approval.
